close_reason: aa82032 clamp de timestamps de frames tras redondeo + fix README
description: Review of FLUJO-AGROMAX-vd5.2 (src/lib/frames-stage.ts) found: computeTimestamps() computes the B-roll window end as durationSeconds-0.5 specifically to avoid extracting a frame at/near the clip's final cutoff. But roundAndDedup() rounds AFTER that window is applied, and Math.round can add up to +0.5s. Worst case (raw timestamp lands exactly on a half-second, e.g. a 25.0s clip's last raw ts of 24.5) the rounded timestamp becomes 25 — equal to the full clip duration, i.e. ffmpeg -ss 25 -i <25s file> seeks to/past EOF. That frame then silently fails extraction and is dropped (per the 'omit failed frame' behavior), quietly reducing the frame count below what was intended, defeating the margin's whole purpose. Reproduced with: node -e computeTimestamps(25.0) -> raw last=24.5, Math.round(24.5)=25 (>= duration). Also, the README.md worked example (lines ~176-188, a 25.0s B-roll clip.mov) shows the manifest ending at 'timeSeconds: 24' but running the actual algorithm on duration 25.0 produces 25, not 24 — the documented example output does not match real code behavior. Expected: either clamp the rounded timestamp to at most floor(durationSeconds)-1 (or similar), or apply the -0.5 safety margin after rounding instead of before, and fix the README example to reflect real output.
title: Fix: B-roll rounding can push last frame timestamp to/past clip duration, defeating the -0.5s margin (from vd5.2)

Because multiple workers call this concurrently, the fs.writeFile calls for progress/prep-progress.json race: Node/libuv gives no ordering guarantee that writes STARTED earlier also COMPLETE earlier. If an earlier-started write (holding an older, smaller snapshot of 'progress') completes AFTER a later-started write (holding a newer, larger snapshot), the file on disk regresses to the stale snapshot and loses the newer clip's status update until the next transition overwrites it again. Impact is limited to UI progress display (X/N proxies, per-clip status) — it does not affect the final proxy .mp4 outputs (tmp+rename there is genuinely atomic per-file) — but a clip could get stuck showing 'pending'/'running' in the UI after it actually finished or errored, until another clip's status change happens to overwrite the file again (or forever if it was the last transition). Suggested fix: serialize prep-progress writes (e.g. a simple write-queue / mutex keyed by jobId) or write with a monotonic version check before persisting.
title: prep-progress.json concurrent pool writes can lose updates (last-completing-write-wins)
